title: 2021 to 2023: Series A to the first Claude
big_idea: Anthropic raised $124 million in 2021 and $580 million in 2022, published its core views on AI safety on 8 March 2023, and on 14 March 2023 offered Claude, an AI assistant, through a chat interface and API.

evidence.quote: Anthropic, an AI safety and research company, has raised $124 million in a Series A.
The Series A round was led by Jaan Tallinn, technology investor and co-founder of Skype.
Anthropic, an AI safety and research company, has raised $580 million in a Series B.
We founded Anthropic because we believe the impact of AI might be comparable to that of the industrial and scientific revolutions, but we aren’t confident it will go well.
We’re offering two versions of Claude today: Claude and Claude Instant.
Accessible through chat interface and API in our developer console, Claude is capable of a wide variety of conversational and text processing tasks

title: 2023 to 2024: Series C to Claude 3.5 Sonnet
big_idea: From May 2023 to June 2024 Anthropic raised $450 million in a Series C, published its Responsible Scaling Policy with AI Safety Levels, and released Claude 2, the Claude 3 family of Haiku, Sonnet and Opus, and Claude 3.5 Sonnet.

evidence.quote: we have raised $450 million in Series C funding led by Spark Capital with participation from Google, Salesforce Ventures, Sound Ventures, Zoom Ventures, and others
Claude 2 has improved performance, longer responses, and can be accessed via API as well as a new public-facing beta website
Users can input up to 100K tokens in each prompt, which means that Claude can work over hundreds of pages of technical documentation or even a book.
Our RSP defines a framework called AI Safety Levels (ASL) for addressing catastrophic risks, modeled loosely after the US government’s biosafety level (BSL) standards
Current LLMs, including Claude, appear to be ASL-2.
The family includes three state-of-the-art models in ascending order of capability: Claude 3 Haiku, Claude 3 Sonnet, and Claude 3 Opus.
Today, we’re launching Claude 3.5 Sonnet—our first release in the forthcoming Claude 3.5 model family.

title: 2024 to 2025: Updated RSP to Claude 4
big_idea: From October 2024 to May 2025 Anthropic published an updated Responsible Scaling Policy, released Claude 3.7 Sonnet together with Claude Code, raised $3.5 billion at a $61.5 billion post-money valuation, introduced Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4, and activated AI Safety Level 3 protections in conjunction with launching Claude Opus 4.

evidence.quote: Today we are publishing a significant update to our Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP), the risk governance framework we use to mitigate potential catastrophic risks from frontier AI systems.
Along with the model, we’re also introducing a command line tool for agentic coding, Claude Code.
Claude Code is available as a limited research preview
Anthropic has raised $3.5 billion at a $61.5 billion post-money valuation.
We have activated the AI Safety Level 3 (ASL-3) Deployment and Security Standards described in Anthropic’s Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) in conjunction with launching Claude Opus 4.
Today, we’re introducing the next generation of Claude models: Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4
Pricing remains consistent with previous Opus and Sonnet models: Opus 4 at $15/$75 per million tokens (input/output) and Sonnet 4 at $3/$15.

title: 2025: Series F to Claude Opus 4.5
big_idea: From September to November 2025 Anthropic raised $13 billion at a $183 billion post-money valuation, announced offices in Bengaluru and Seoul and opened one in Tokyo, named Rahul Patil Chief Technology Officer, reported an AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign it detected in mid-September 2025, and released Claude Opus 4.5.

evidence.quote: Anthropic has completed a Series F fundraising of $13 billion led by ICONIQ. This financing values Anthropic at $183 billion post-money.
we’re expanding our global operations to India, with plans to open an office in Bengaluru in early 2026.
We're excited to announce that Rahul Patil has joined Anthropic as our Chief Technology Officer.
Most recently, he served as CTO of Stripe, where he guided the technical organization supporting millions of businesses
Today we're announcing plans to open an office in Seoul in early 2026 as our global operations expand into Korea.
This week, we opened our first Asia-Pacific office in Tokyo, a milestone in Anthropic's international expansion.
In mid-September 2025, we detected suspicious activity that later investigation determined to be a highly sophisticated espionage campaign.
Our newest model, Claude Opus 4.5, is available today.
Pricing is now $5/$25 per million tokens—making Opus-level capabilities accessible to even more users, teams, and enterprises.

title: 2026: Series G to the third RSP
big_idea: In February and March 2026 Anthropic raised $30 billion at a $380 billion post-money valuation, identified distillation campaigns by DeepSeek, Moonshot and MiniMax, released the third version of its Responsible Scaling Policy, and announced a Sydney office as its fourth in Asia-Pacific.

evidence.quote: We have raised $30 billion in Series G funding led by GIC and Coatue, valuing Anthropic at $380 billion post-money.
We have identified industrial-scale campaigns by three AI laboratories—DeepSeek, Moonshot, and MiniMax—to illicitly extract Claude’s capabilities to improve their own models.
These labs generated over 16 million exchanges with Claude through approximately 24,000 fraudulent accounts, in violation of our terms of service and regional access restrictions.
We’re releasing the third version of our Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP), the voluntary framework we use to mitigate catastrophic risks from AI systems.
In the coming weeks, we will open an office in Sydney—our fourth office in Asia-Pacific, alongside Tokyo, Bengaluru, and Seoul.

title: 2026: Project Glasswing to Claude Opus 5
big_idea: From May to October 2026 Anthropic reported that approximately 50 partners had used Claude Mythos Preview to find more than ten thousand high- or critical-severity vulnerabilities, extended Project Glasswing to approximately 150 new organizations, raised $65 billion at a $965 billion post-money valuation, launched Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, made Claude Opus 5 available, and announced a Singapore office and a government MOU.

evidence.quote: approximately 50 partners have used Claude Mythos Preview to find more than ten thousand high- or critical-severity vulnerabilities across the most systemically important software in the world
we announced that roughly 50 initial partners had access to Claude Mythos Preview
Project Glasswing is our collaborative effort to secure the world’s most important software.
we’re extending the partnership to approximately 150 new organizations. Each one will need to meet our security requirements before they gain access.
Anthropic has raised $65 billion in Series H funding led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia Capital, valuing the company at $965 billion post-money.
It’s the same underlying model as Fable 5, but with the safeguards lifted in some areas.
Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are being offered at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens—less than half the price of Claude Mythos Preview.
Today’s joint launch is another step towards our goal of bringing advanced AI capabilities to as many users as possible
Claude Opus 5 is available today on all platforms, priced at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens

we are expanding our Asia-Pacific operations by opening a new office in Singapore—our fifth in the region—and signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Singapore Ministry of Digital Development and Information.
